A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PalmBench. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original device measurements of memory, utilization, throughput, energy, and temperature, alongside evaluations of quantized-model accuracy, hallucination, and toxicity.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical evaluations and adds phase-specific throughput, component memory breakdowns, layer-wise GPU measurements, and additional device energy and temperature results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same automated MLC/llama.cpp benchmarking approach and existing quantization methods. V2 names and explains the Evaluator, Scheduler, and Profiling and Monitor modules without establishing a change to the underlying algorithm or workflow.

E1.justification: The datasets, language tasks, and mobile/edge platform coverage are retained. Orange Pi and Jetson already appear in v1 evaluations; adding their energy and temperature entries expands reported measurements rather than introducing a new platform or task.

E2.justification: The evaluated model, inference-engine, and quantization comparator sets are retained, including GPTQ, AWQ, ggml/K-quant, and FasterTransformer. Newly discussed MobileAIBench, Starting Kit, and RTN comparisons concern prior literature, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 introduces component-level memory evaluation and GPU profiling across two transformer blocks of Llama-3-8B on Pixel 7, extending the evaluation design. Existing experiments retain the stated 0.2 temperature and 4096-token context; newly supplied reset, OS, and sampling details do not establish that those experiments changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's aggregate resource measurements and timelines, v2 Figures 11–12 add substantial diagnostic analyses: memory decompositions into weights, KV cache, activations, and overhead; self-attention versus FFN utilization; and a Phi2/Mistral memory comparison. These investigate internal bottlenecks and architecture-dependent resource costs.

E5.justification: V2 Section 4.1 newly states that all experiments were repeated ten times, and Figure 11(b) adds percentage variability annotations. V1 supplies neither practice. The annotations are not defined as standard deviations or confidence intervals, and the newly disclosed repetition count does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include prefill/decode measurements in Figure 7, memory and layer profiles in Figures 11–12, and Orange Pi/Jetson entries in Table 3. Figure 12 reports 6.1 GB for Mistral-7B 3-bit versus 4.2 GB for Phi2 4-bit. Earlier overall throughput is retained as Figure 13, and Tables 4–5 remain numerically unchanged. V2 also removes the claim that 3-bit produces more hallucinations than 2-bit, which those retained tables contradict.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations. The added sampling explanations are informal descriptions of standard decoding options.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims: automated mobile benchmarking, resource-efficiency comparisons, quantization quality and harmful-output evaluation, and favorable iOS efficiency and throughput. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 identifies self-attention as a potential GPU bottleneck and recommends optimizing attention and matrix multiplication. It also links Phi2's suitability to lower total memory including KV cache, explains thermal imaging's value for locating hotspots, and adds decoding-support limitations.

D1.justification: V2 adds OS versions, factory-reset preparation, nucleus/top-p and optional top-k settings, btop/jetson-stats instrumentation, the Klein Tools power-meter supplier, and clearer module responsibilities. Code release remains a future plan. Appendix A.1 inconsistently states temperatures of 0.2 and 0.4, leaving the added configuration documentation partly ambiguous.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of MobileAIBench and the Edge-Device LLM Competition Starting Kit, plus quantization studies and on-device/model-compression surveys. These refine positioning around automation, cross-platform evaluation, and layer-wise profiling while retaining the existing research gap and principal contribution.

P1.justification: Several related-work, automation, and experimental-discussion paragraphs are rewritten. The Infrastructure heading is removed and its subsections regrouped under Choice of LLMs; appendix organization and author/affiliation text also change. The overall narrative and main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn to explain datasets and framework modules. V2 adds a four-panel prefill/decode figure and component/layer analysis figures, relocates the old throughput chart to Appendix Figure 13, and expands Table 3 with edge-device columns. These substantially extend the visual presentation beyond routine reflow.

improvement.justification: The component analyses and clearer workflow make v1's largely aggregate resource discussion more informative, while added experimental details improve assessability. Removing the incorrect 3-bit hallucination comparison also improves consistency with Tables 4–5. Benefits are limited by conflicting temperature settings, Figure 7's inconsistent Llama2 quantization labels, and undefined variability annotations. The net improvement is useful but limited.
